column1: Filter bar is shown below the tab row on the Work Orders page
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. At least a few work orders exist in the shop.
column6:
1. Open the Work Orders page.
2. Look at the area directly under the tab row (All, Estimates, Completed, My Work Orders).
column7:
1. A filter bar is visible directly below the tab row and above the work order table.
2. The filter bar is shown by default (expanded) without having to turn anything on.

column1: Five filter chips appear in a fixed order, each with an icon, its name and a down arrow
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the filter bar visible.
column6:
1. Read the filter chips in the filter bar from left to right.
2. Look at what each chip shows.
column7:
1. Exactly five filter chips appear, in this order: Status, Customer, Lead Technician, Service Advisor, Asset on site.
2. Each chip shows a small icon, the filter name and a down arrow (chevron) indicating it opens a dropdown.
3. In the design the icons are: a spinner for Status, a person for Customer, a wrench for Lead Technician, a headset for Service Advisor and a truck for Asset on site.

column1: The filter bar still shows the remaining chips on a tab where the Status filter is hidden
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
column6:
1. Click the Estimates tab.
2. Look at the filter bar.
column7:
1. The filter bar is still shown (it does not disappear).
2. The remaining filter chips (Customer, Lead Technician, Service Advisor, Asset on site) are displayed and usable.

column1: Status chip opens a checkbox list of all nine work order statuses with a Clear selection action
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All or My Work Orders tab.
3. No filters are currently selected.
column6:
1. Click the Status filter chip.
2. Read the list of options from top to bottom.
3. Look at the bottom of the dropdown panel.
column7:
1. A dropdown panel opens under the Status chip.
2. It lists all nine statuses as checkboxes, in this order: Estimate, Approved, In progress, Review, Complete, Invoiced, Paid, Declined, Imported.
3. All checkboxes are unticked (nothing selected yet).
4. A 'Clear selection' action is shown at the bottom of the dropdown.

column1: Ticking one status filters the table immediately, with no apply button
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. Work orders exist in at least two different statuses (for example some Estimate and some Approved - create ZZAUTOTEST work orders if needed).
column6:
1. Click the Status filter chip.
2. Tick the checkbox for one status (for example Estimate).
3. Watch the work order table while the dropdown is still open.
column7:
1. The ticked checkbox appears filled (checked).
2. The table updates immediately to show only work orders in the selected status - there is no confirm or apply button on desktop.
3. Work orders in other statuses are no longer listed.

column1: Ticking several statuses shows work orders matching any of them
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. Work orders exist in at least three different statuses (seed ZZAUTOTEST work orders if needed).
column6:
1. Click the Status filter chip.
2. Tick two or more statuses (for example Estimate and Approved).
3. Look at the work order table.
column7:
1. Every ticked status shows a filled checkbox.
2. The table shows work orders whose status matches ANY of the ticked statuses (both Estimate and Approved rows appear).
3. Work orders in statuses that are not ticked are hidden.
4. There is no limit on how many statuses you can tick.
column8: requirements.md Story 2 S2-R2; §4 Key Decisions (no selection limit)

column1: Clear selection in the Status dropdown unticks every status and removes the filter
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. Two or more statuses are ticked in the Status filter and the table is filtered.
column6:
1. Open the Status dropdown (if it is not already open).
2. Click 'Clear selection' at the bottom of the dropdown.
3. Look at the checkboxes and the table.
column7:
1. All status checkboxes become unticked.
2. The Status filter is removed and the table returns to showing work orders of every status.
3. Only the Status filter is affected - any other active filters stay applied.

column1: Clicking outside the Status dropdown closes it and keeps the selections applied
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. The Status dropdown is open with at least one status ticked.
column6:
1. Click anywhere outside the open dropdown (for example on empty page space).
2. Look at the dropdown, the Status chip and the table.
column7:
1. The dropdown closes.
2. The ticked statuses stay selected - the Status chip stays in its active state showing the selection.
3. The table stays filtered by the selected statuses.

column1: Selecting statuses that no work order has shows the empty state
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. At least one status exists that NO current work order has (for example Imported - check the list first).
column6:
1. Click the Status filter chip.
2. Tick only the status that no work order currently has.
3. Look at the table area.
column7:
1. The table shows no rows.
2. An empty state is displayed saying no results were found for the current filters (see the Empty State cases for its full content).
3. The app does not show an error.

column1: Customer chip opens a dropdown with a 'Search customer' field and a scrollable customer list
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
3. Several customers exist in the shop.
column6:
1. Click the Customer filter chip.
2. Look at the top of the dropdown panel and the list below it.
3. Look at the bottom of the panel.
column7:
1. A dropdown panel opens under the Customer chip.
2. A search input with the placeholder 'Search customer' is at the top, already focused so you can type right away.
3. Below it is a scrollable list of customer names.
4. A 'Clear selection' action is shown at the bottom of the panel.

column1: Typing in the customer search narrows the list to matching names
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the Customer dropdown open.
3. Several customers with different names exist.
column6:
1. Type part of one customer's name into the 'Search customer' field (for example the first few letters).
2. Watch the list while you type.
column7:
1. The customer list narrows as you type, showing only names that match what you entered.
2. Customers that do not match are removed from the list.
3. Deleting the text brings the full list back.

column1: Selecting customers adds removable tags in the dropdown input area and checkmarks in the list
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the Customer dropdown open.
3. At least three customers exist.
column6:
1. Click one customer in the list.
2. Click a second and a third customer.
3. Look at the input area at the top of the dropdown and at the list rows.
column7:
1. Each selected customer appears as a tag (small chip) with an x in the input area at the top of the dropdown.
2. Each selected customer's row in the list shows a checkmark on the right.
3. Long customer names on tags are shortened with an ellipsis (for example 'Texas Truck And Aut...').
4. You can keep selecting as many customers as needed - there is no selection limit.
column8: requirements.md Story 3 S3-R3; S3-R4; §4 Key Decisions (no selection limit)

column1: Clicking the x on a customer tag removes just that customer from the selection
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the Customer dropdown open.
3. Two or more customers are selected (their tags are visible in the input area).
column6:
1. Click the x on one selected customer's tag.
2. Look at the tags, the list and the work order table.
column7:
1. That customer's tag disappears from the input area.
2. The checkmark next to that customer in the list is removed.
3. The other selected customers keep their tags and checkmarks.
4. The table updates to no longer include that customer's work orders.

column1: The table shows only work orders belonging to any of the selected customers
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. At least two customers each have at least one work order, and a third customer's work orders also exist (seed ZZAUTOTEST data if needed).
column6:
1. Open the Customer filter and select two customers.
2. Look at the Customer column in the work order table.
column7:
1. The table shows only work orders whose customer is one of the two selected customers.
2. Work orders belonging to any other customer are hidden.
3. The table updates in real time as you make the selections (no apply button on desktop).
column8: requirements.md Story 3 S3-R6; Story 2 S2-R6 (real-time pattern)

column1: Clear selection in the Customer dropdown removes all selected customers
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
3. Two or more customers are selected in the Customer filter and the table is filtered.
column6:
1. Open the Customer dropdown (if not already open).
2. Click 'Clear selection' at the bottom of the dropdown.
3. Look at the tags, the list and the table.
column7:
1. All customer tags are removed from the input area.
2. All checkmarks in the list are removed.
3. The Customer filter is removed and the table shows work orders of all customers again.
4. Other active filters (if any) are not affected.

column1: Clicking outside the Customer dropdown closes it and the selections remain
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the Customer dropdown open and two customers selected.
column6:
1. Click anywhere outside the dropdown.
2. Look at the Customer chip and the table.
3. Click the Customer chip again to reopen the dropdown.
column7:
1. The dropdown closes when you click outside it.
2. The Customer chip stays in the active (blue) state showing the selection and the table stays filtered.
3. When reopened, the selected customers' tags are still visible in the input area.

column1: Customer search with no matching name shows a no-results message in the list
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the Customer dropdown open.
column6:
1. Type a string that matches no customer name (for example 'zzzqqq').
2. Look at the list area of the dropdown.
column7:
1. The list shows a message saying there are no results (instead of an empty gap).
2. The app does not show an error.
3. Clearing the search text brings the customer list back.

column1: A customer with no open work orders is still listed; filtering by them returns an empty result
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. A customer exists who currently has NO work orders (create a fresh ZZAUTOTEST customer if needed).
3. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
column6:
1. Open the Customer filter and search for the customer who has no work orders.
2. Confirm they appear in the list, then select them (and only them).
3. Look at the table.
column7:
1. The customer with no work orders IS shown in the filter list (they are not hidden).
2. After selecting only that customer, the table shows no rows and the filtered empty state is displayed.
3. No error is shown.
column8: requirements.md Story 3 S3-E1; S3-N2; Story 8 S8-R3

column1: Lead Technician chip opens a dropdown with a 'Search technician' field and a technician list
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
3. Several technicians exist in the shop.
column6:
1. Click the Lead Technician filter chip.
2. Look at the top of the dropdown, the list below and the bottom of the panel.
column7:
1. A dropdown panel opens under the Lead Technician chip.
2. A search input with the placeholder 'Search technician' is at the top.
3. Below it is a scrollable list of technician names.
4. A 'Clear selection' action is shown at the bottom.

column1: Typing in the technician search narrows the list to matching names
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the Lead Technician dropdown open.
column6:
1. Type part of one technician's name into the 'Search technician' field.
2. Watch the list while you type.
column7:
1. The technician list narrows to only the names matching what you typed.
2. Deleting the text brings the full list back.

column1: Selecting technicians shows only work orders where they are the lead technician
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. Work orders exist with different lead technicians assigned, including at least one work order where the chosen technician is assigned but NOT as lead (seed ZZAUTOTEST data if needed).
column6:
1. Open the Lead Technician filter and select one or two technicians.
2. Look at the checkboxes in the list and the work order table.
column7:
1. Selected technicians show a filled checkbox in the list.
2. The table shows only work orders where one of the selected technicians is assigned as the LEAD technician.
3. A work order where the technician is assigned only in a non-lead role does not appear.
4. The table updates in real time as you select.

column1: Clear selection in the Lead Technician dropdown removes all selected technicians
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
3. One or more technicians are selected in the Lead Technician filter.
column6:
1. Open the Lead Technician dropdown and click 'Clear selection' at the bottom.
2. Look at the list and the table.
column7:
1. All technician selections are removed (checkboxes unticked).
2. The Lead Technician filter no longer restricts the table.
3. Other active filters are not affected.

column1: Clicking outside the Lead Technician dropdown closes it
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the Lead Technician dropdown open and one technician selected.
column6:
1. Click anywhere outside the dropdown.
2. Look at the dropdown, the chip and the table.
column7:
1. The dropdown closes.
2. The selection stays applied - the chip stays active and the table stays filtered.

column1: Selecting a technician who leads no work orders shows the empty state
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. A technician exists who is not the lead technician on ANY work order (create a fresh ZZAUTOTEST staff member if needed).
3. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab with no other filters active.
column6:
1. Open the Lead Technician filter and select only that technician.
2. Look at the table.
column7:
1. The table shows no rows and the filtered empty state is displayed.
2. No error is shown.

column1: A deactivated technician does not appear in the Lead Technician filter list
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. A test technician (ZZAUTOTEST) exists and is visible in the Lead Technician filter list.
3. That test technician is then made inactive/deactivated in staff administration (restore them afterwards).
column6:
1. On the Work Orders page, open the Lead Technician filter.
2. Search for the deactivated technician's name.
3. Look at the list.
column7:
1. The deactivated technician is NOT shown in the filter list.
2. Active technicians are still listed normally.

column1: Service Advisor chip opens a dropdown with a 'Search advisor' field and an advisor list
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
3. Several service advisors exist in the shop.
column6:
1. Click the Service Advisor filter chip.
2. Look at the top of the dropdown, the list below and the bottom of the panel.
column7:
1. A dropdown panel opens under the Service Advisor chip.
2. A search input with the placeholder 'Search advisor' is at the top.
3. Below it is a scrollable list of advisor names.
4. A 'Clear selection' action is shown at the bottom.

column1: Typing in the advisor search narrows the list to matching names
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the Service Advisor dropdown open.
column6:
1. Type part of one advisor's name into the 'Search advisor' field.
2. Watch the list while you type.
column7:
1. The advisor list narrows to only the names matching what you typed.
2. Deleting the text brings the full list back.

column1: Selecting advisors shows only work orders assigned to those advisors
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. Work orders exist with different service advisors assigned (seed ZZAUTOTEST data if needed).
column6:
1. Open the Service Advisor filter and select one or two advisors.
2. Look at the checkboxes in the list and the Service Advisor column in the table.
column7:
1. Selected advisors show a filled checkbox in the list.
2. The table shows only work orders assigned to any of the selected advisors.
3. The table updates in real time as you select.

column1: Clear selection in the Service Advisor dropdown removes all selected advisors
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
3. One or more advisors are selected in the Service Advisor filter.
column6:
1. Open the Service Advisor dropdown and click 'Clear selection' at the bottom.
2. Look at the list and the table.
column7:
1. All advisor selections are removed.
2. The Service Advisor filter no longer restricts the table.
3. Other active filters are not affected.

column1: Clicking outside the Service Advisor dropdown closes it
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the Service Advisor dropdown open and one advisor selected.
column6:
1. Click anywhere outside the dropdown.
2. Look at the dropdown, the chip and the table.
column7:
1. The dropdown closes.
2. The selection stays applied - the chip stays active and the table stays filtered.

column1: Selecting an advisor with no assigned work orders shows the empty state
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. An advisor exists who is not assigned to ANY work order (create a fresh ZZAUTOTEST staff member if needed).
3. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab with no other filters active.
column6:
1. Open the Service Advisor filter and select only that advisor.
2. Look at the table.
column7:
1. The table shows no rows and the filtered empty state is displayed.
2. No error is shown.

column1: A deactivated advisor does not appear in the Service Advisor filter list
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. A test advisor (ZZAUTOTEST) exists and is visible in the Service Advisor filter list.
3. That test advisor is then made inactive/deactivated in staff administration (restore them afterwards).
column6:
1. On the Work Orders page, open the Service Advisor filter.
2. Search for the deactivated advisor's name.
3. Look at the list.
column7:
1. The deactivated advisor is NOT shown in the filter list.
2. Active advisors are still listed normally.

column1: Asset on site chip opens a dropdown with exactly two options, Yes and No, plus Clear selection
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
column6:
1. Click the Asset on site filter chip.
2. Read the options in the dropdown.
column7:
1. A small dropdown panel opens under the Asset on site chip.
2. It contains exactly two options: Yes and No.
3. A 'Clear selection' action is shown at the bottom.
4. It is a dropdown (like the other filters), not an on/off toggle.
column8: requirements.md Story 6 S6-R1; §4 Key Decisions (dropdown, not toggle)

column1: Choosing Yes shows only work orders whose asset is on site
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. Work orders exist in both states: some with the asset marked on site and some not (set the on-site marker on ZZAUTOTEST work orders as needed).
column6:
1. Open the Asset on site filter and choose Yes.
2. Look at the On Site column in the table (green house icon = on site, red = not).
column7:
1. The table shows only work orders whose asset is currently on site.
2. Work orders whose asset is not on site are hidden.
3. Choosing No instead shows only the not-on-site work orders.

column1: Asset on site is single-select: choosing the other option replaces the first
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with Yes selected in the Asset on site filter.
column6:
1. Open the Asset on site dropdown again.
2. Choose No.
3. Look at the selection and the table.
column7:
1. No becomes the selected option and Yes is deselected automatically - only one option can be selected at a time.
2. The table switches to showing only the not-on-site work orders.
3. The chip shows the currently selected value.

column1: Clear selection in the Asset on site dropdown removes the filter
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with Yes or No selected in the Asset on site filter.
column6:
1. Open the Asset on site dropdown and click 'Clear selection'.
2. Look at the chip and the table.
column7:
1. The selection is removed and the chip returns to its default (inactive) state.
2. The table shows work orders regardless of on-site status again.
3. Other active filters are not affected.

column1: Clicking outside the Asset on site dropdown closes it
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the Asset on site dropdown open and Yes selected.
column6:
1. Click anywhere outside the dropdown.
2. Look at the dropdown, the chip and the table.
column7:
1. The dropdown closes.
2. The Yes selection stays applied - the chip stays active and the table stays filtered.

column1: An Asset on site choice that matches no work orders shows the empty state
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab with no other filters active.
3. Every current work order is in the SAME on-site state (set all ZZAUTOTEST work orders to on site, or combine with another filter so one option matches nothing).
column6:
1. Open the Asset on site filter and choose the option that matches no work orders (for example No when everything is on site).
2. Look at the table.
column7:
1. The table shows no rows and the filtered empty state is displayed.
2. No error is shown.

column1: A chip with a selected value turns into the active blue state and shows the value
column2: Active Filter Chips and Clear Filters
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with no filters selected (all chips in their default grey state).
column6:
1. Open the Status filter and tick one status (for example Estimate).
2. Click outside to close the dropdown and look at the Status chip.
column7:
1. The Status chip changes to an active/highlighted look (blue pill).
2. The chip displays the selected value (for example 'Status: Estimate').
3. The other chips stay in their default state.

column1: A chip with several values shows the first values and shortens the rest with an ellipsis
column2: Active Filter Chips and Clear Filters
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
column6:
1. Open the Status filter and tick three or more statuses (for example Estimate, In progress and Approved).
2. Close the dropdown and read the Status chip label.
column7:
1. The chip lists the selected values starting with the first one and shortens the label when it gets too long (the design shows 'Status: Estimate, In progress, Approved...').
2. The chip stays a single compact pill - it does not grow to show every value in full.

column1: 'Clear filters' appears to the right of the chips only when at least one filter is active
column2: Active Filter Chips and Clear Filters
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with no filters selected.
column6:
1. Look at the right end of the filter chip row with no filters active.
2. Select any filter value (for example one status).
3. Look at the right end of the chip row again.
4. Remove the selection (Clear selection in the dropdown) and look once more.
column7:
1. With no filters active, no 'Clear filters' button/link is shown (there is nothing to click).
2. As soon as one filter is active, a blue 'Clear filters' link appears at the right end of the chip row.
3. When the last active filter is removed, 'Clear filters' disappears again.
column8: requirements.md Story 7 S7-R3; S7-N1; Story 8 S8-N1

column1: 'Clear filters' removes every active filter at once and all chips return to default
column2: Active Filter Chips and Clear Filters
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. Values are selected in at least three different filters (for example a status, a customer and Asset on site Yes).
column6:
1. Click the 'Clear filters' link at the right end of the chip row.
2. Look at all the chips and the table.
column7:
1. Every active filter is cleared in one click.
2. All chips return to their default (inactive) look with no values shown.
3. The table shows the full unfiltered list again.
4. The 'Clear filters' link disappears.

column1: 'Clear selection' inside one dropdown clears only that filter and leaves the others active
column2: Active Filter Chips and Clear Filters
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. Values are selected in at least two different filters (for example a status and a customer).
column6:
1. Open the Status dropdown and click 'Clear selection'.
2. Look at the Status chip, the Customer chip and the table.
column7:
1. Only the Status filter is cleared - its chip returns to default.
2. The Customer filter stays selected and active (blue) and keeps filtering the table.
3. 'Clear filters' remains visible because a filter is still active.

column1: Several different filters combine: only work orders matching every active filter remain
column2: Active Filter Chips and Clear Filters
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. Seed ZZAUTOTEST work orders so that: customer A has an Estimate work order and an Approved work order, and customer B has an Estimate work order.
column6:
1. Open the Status filter and tick Estimate.
2. Open the Customer filter and select customer A.
3. Look at the table.
column7:
1. Only customer A's Estimate work order is shown.
2. Customer A's Approved work order is hidden (wrong status) and customer B's Estimate work order is hidden (wrong customer) - each additional filter narrows the result further.
3. Both chips are in the active state and 'Clear filters' is visible.
column8: requirements.md §2 Feature Overview (multi-criteria); Story 8 S8-R3 ('combination of active filters')

column1: The toolbar funnel button collapses the filter bar and the table reclaims the space
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the filter bar visible (expanded).
column6:
1. Find the filter (funnel) icon button in the page toolbar (next to the Search magnifier and the column/layout toggle, left of the New Work Order button).
2. Click the funnel icon once.
3. Look at the filter bar area and the table.
column7:
1. The filter bar row is hidden.
2. The work order table moves up and uses the reclaimed vertical space.
3. The funnel icon shows a pressed/active look while the bar is collapsed.

column1: Expanding the filter bar brings it back exactly as it was, with active filters still shown
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
3. At least one filter is selected (for example two statuses) and the filter bar has been collapsed with the funnel button.
column6:
1. Click the funnel icon in the toolbar again.
2. Look at the filter bar.
column7:
1. The filter bar reappears below the tab row.
2. The previously selected filters are still shown on their chips in the active (blue) state - nothing was lost while collapsed.
3. The 'Clear filters' link is still shown at the right end of the chip row.

column1: The collapsed or expanded state of the filter bar is remembered after leaving and returning
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page and have collapsed the filter bar with the funnel button.
column6:
1. Navigate to another page (for example open a work order, or go to Customers).
2. Return to the Work Orders page.
3. Look at the filter bar area.
4. Expand the bar with the funnel button, leave the page again and come back.
column7:
1. After step 2 the filter bar is still collapsed (your choice was remembered).
2. After step 4 the filter bar is expanded again when you return - whichever state you left it in is restored.

column1: The funnel button shows a blue indicator when filters are active while the bar is collapsed, and none when no filters are active
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
column6:
1. With NO filters selected, collapse the filter bar with the funnel button and look at the funnel icon.
2. Expand the bar, select at least one filter value (for example a status).
3. Collapse the bar again and look at the funnel icon.
column7:
1. After step 1 the funnel icon shows no special indicator (only its normal pressed look).
2. After step 3 the funnel icon shows a visual indicator (filters icon in primary blue) signalling that active filters are in effect while the bar is hidden.

column1: Active filters keep filtering the table while the filter bar is collapsed
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. Work orders exist in several statuses; a Status filter is applied (for example Estimate only) and the table is visibly filtered.
column6:
1. Collapse the filter bar with the funnel button.
2. Look at the work order table.
column7:
1. The table content does not change when the bar collapses - it still shows only the work orders matching the active filters.
2. Hiding the bar only hides the chips; it does not remove or pause the filtering.

column1: A filter combination with no matching work orders shows a no-results empty state instead of a blank table
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. Work orders exist, but you can pick a filter combination that matches none of them (for example a customer plus a status that customer never has).
column6:
1. Apply the filter combination that matches no work orders.
2. Look at the table area.
column7:
1. The table body is replaced by an empty state (not just a bare empty grid).
2. The empty state shows a message indicating no results were found for the current filters.
3. No error message or broken layout appears.

column1: The filtered empty state offers a way to clear the filters, and using it brings the list back
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page showing the filtered empty state (a filter combination matching no work orders is applied).
column6:
1. Read the empty state content.
2. Click the clear-filters prompt/link inside the empty state.
3. Look at the table and the chips.
column7:
1. The empty state includes a prompt or link to clear the filters.
2. Clicking it removes the active filters and the full work order list is shown again.
3. The chips return to their default state.

column1: The All tab shows all five filter chips, all working
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
column6:
1. Click the All tab.
2. Count the filter chips and click each one briefly.
column7:
1. All five chips are shown: Status, Customer, Lead Technician, Service Advisor, Asset on site.
2. Each chip opens its dropdown and can be used.

column1: On the Estimates tab the Status filter is not offered; the other four filters work on top of the Estimates pre-filter
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. Estimate work orders exist for at least two different customers.
3. You are on the Work Orders page.
column6:
1. Click the Estimates tab.
2. Look at the filter bar.
3. Open the Customer filter and select one customer.
4. Look at the table.
column7:
1. The Status filter is not offered as a usable filter on this tab (per the spec the chip is hidden; the tab already pre-filters to Estimate).
2. Customer, Lead Technician, Service Advisor and Asset on site chips are shown and usable.
3. After step 3 the table shows only that customer's ESTIMATE work orders - the customer filter narrows the pre-filtered Estimates list.
column8: requirements.md Story 9 S9-R2; Story 2 S2-N1; §4 Key Decisions

column1: On the Completed tab the Status filter is not offered; the other four filters work on top of the Completed pre-filter
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. Complete work orders exist for at least two different customers.
3. You are on the Work Orders page.
column6:
1. Click the Completed tab.
2. Look at the filter bar.
3. Open the Customer filter and select one customer.
4. Look at the table.
column7:
1. The Status filter is not offered as a usable filter on this tab (the tab already pre-filters to Complete).
2. Customer, Lead Technician, Service Advisor and Asset on site chips are shown and usable.
3. After step 3 the table shows only that customer's COMPLETE work orders.
column8: requirements.md Story 9 S9-R3; Story 2 S2-N2; §4 Key Decisions

column1: On the My Work Orders tab all five filters are shown and narrow the already user-scoped list
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. Work orders assigned to you exist in at least two statuses, and other users' work orders also exist.
3. You are on the Work Orders page.
column6:
1. Click the My Work Orders tab and count the chips.
2. Open the Status filter and tick one status your work orders have.
3. Look at the table.
column7:
1. All five filter chips are shown on the My Work Orders tab.
2. The table only ever shows work orders assigned to you (the tab's own scope stays).
3. After step 2 it shows only YOUR work orders in the ticked status - the filters narrow the user-scoped list, they do not widen it to other users' work orders.
column8: requirements.md Story 9 S9-R4; §4 Key Decisions (My Work Orders tab does not remove filters)

column1: Filter selections survive tab switching; a Status selection hidden on Estimates/Completed comes back on the All tab
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. A Status selection (for example Approved) and a Customer selection are active.
column6:
1. Click the Estimates tab and look at the filter bar and the table.
2. Click back to the All tab and look again.
column7:
1. On the Estimates tab the Status selection is not applied and not shown as an editable filter (incompatible with the tab), but the Customer selection is still shown and still filters the list.
2. Back on the All tab the Status chip reappears with the SAME selection (Approved) still applied - the selection was retained in memory, not lost.
3. The Customer selection is unchanged throughout.

column1: Leaving the Work Orders page and coming back restores the filters and the bar state exactly
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with a Status and a Customer selection active and the filter bar expanded.
column6:
1. Open one work order from the list (go to its detail page).
2. Go back to the Work Orders page.
3. Look at the chips, the table and the filter bar state.
4. Repeat the round-trip once more with the filter bar collapsed before leaving.
column7:
1. After step 2 the same Status and Customer selections are still applied - chips active with the same values, table filtered the same way.
2. The filter bar is still expanded (as you left it).
3. After step 4 the filter bar comes back collapsed - the collapsed/expanded state is restored too.

column1: Filter selections persist while the browser session lasts, wherever you go in the app
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. Filters are applied on the Work Orders page (for example a status and a customer).
column6:
1. Visit several other areas of the app (Customers, Parts, Reports) and use them briefly.
2. Return to the Work Orders page.
3. Look at the chips and the table.
column7: 1. The filter selections are still applied after moving around the app - you do not have to re-apply them within the same browser session.
column8: requirements.md Story 10 S10-R2; §2/§4 (persist across navigation, saved per user)

column1: Saved filters are per user: one user's filters do not appear for another user
column5:
1. Two test users (A and B) can sign in to the same shop.
2. User A has applied filters on the Work Orders page (for example Status: Approved).
column6:
1. As user B (separate login/browser profile), open the Work Orders page.
2. Look at the filter chips and the table.
3. As user B, apply a DIFFERENT filter (for example a customer), then re-check user A's view.
column7:
1. User B does not see user A's filters - user B's page opens with user B's own (or no) filters.
2. User B's new filter does not change what user A sees; each user keeps their own saved filter state.
column8: requirements.md Story 10 S10-R3; §4 Key Decisions (saved per user)

column1: A remembered filter value that no longer exists is silently dropped when you return
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. A throwaway ZZAUTOTEST customer exists and is selected in the Customer filter together with one real customer.
3. You then navigate away and the ZZAUTOTEST customer is deleted (or otherwise removed) while you are off the page.
column6:
1. Return to the Work Orders page.
2. Look at the Customer chip, the dropdown and the table.
column7:
1. The deleted customer is silently ignored - no error or warning appears.
2. The Customer filter now reflects only the still-valid selection (the real customer).
3. The table is filtered by the remaining valid selection only.

column1: Applying filters updates the page URL to reflect the active filter state
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with no filters applied; note the current URL.
column6:
1. Apply a Status selection and a Customer selection.
2. Look at the browser address bar.
3. Clear all filters and look at the address bar again.
column7:
1. After step 1 the URL changes to include the active filter state.
2. After step 3 the filter part of the URL is removed again.

column1: Opening a shared or bookmarked URL loads the Work Orders page with those filters already applied
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You have copied a Work Orders URL that was produced with filters applied (for example Status: Approved + one customer).
column6:
1. Open the copied URL in a new browser tab (same signed-in user).
2. Look at the chips and the table as the page loads.
column7:
1. The page opens with the same filters already applied - chips active with the same values.
2. The table is already filtered accordingly on load (no need to re-apply anything).
3. The same works from a saved bookmark.
column8: requirements.md Story 11 S11-R2; §2 Feature Overview (share or bookmark)

column1: A URL containing a filter value that no longer exists loads without that value
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You saved a filtered Work Orders URL that includes a throwaway ZZAUTOTEST customer plus one real filter value.
3. The ZZAUTOTEST customer has since been deleted.
column6:
1. Open the saved URL.
2. Look at the chips and the table.
column7:
1. The page loads normally - no error.
2. The deleted value is ignored; only the still-valid filter value is applied and shown on the chips.
3. The table reflects only the valid filter.

column1: A malformed filter URL loads the page unfiltered without showing an error
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You have a valid filtered Work Orders URL to start from.
column6:
1. Manually break the filter part of the URL (for example scramble the parameter values or insert nonsense text).
2. Open the broken URL.
3. Look at the page, the chips and the table.
column7:
1. The Work Orders page loads normally.
2. No filters are applied (chips in default state, full list shown) - the unrecognizable state is discarded.
3. No error message or broken page appears.

column1: On mobile the filter chips sit in a horizontally scrollable row below the tabs, starting with All Filters
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device (or a mobile-size browser window).
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
column6:
1. Look at the row below the tab row (All, Estimates, Completed, My Work Orders).
2. Swipe the chip row sideways.
column7:
1. A filter chip row is shown below the tabs, starting with an 'All Filters' chip (with a funnel icon) followed by the individual filter chips (Status, Customer, Lead Technician, ...).
2. The row scrolls horizontally - chips that do not fit are reachable by swiping.
3. A right-edge arrow affordance indicates the row can be scrolled (per the design variant).

column1: Tapping All Filters opens a bottom sheet listing every filter as an expandable row with an Apply filters button
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
column6:
1. Tap the 'All Filters' chip.
2. Read the sheet from top to bottom.
column7:
1. A bottom sheet slides up with a drag handle at the top, the centered title 'All Filters' and a close (x) button.
2. It lists the five filters as expandable accordion rows, each with its icon, name and a down arrow: Status, Customer, Lead Technician, Service Advisor, Asset on site.
3. A sticky blue 'Apply filters' button sits at the bottom of the sheet.

column1: Selecting statuses in the mobile sheet and tapping Apply filters filters the list and counts on the sheet title
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab; work orders exist in several statuses.
3. The 'All Filters' bottom sheet is open.
column6:
1. Tap the Status accordion row to expand it.
2. Tick one or more statuses.
3. Tap the 'Apply filters' button.
4. Reopen the All Filters sheet and look at its title.
column7:
1. Expanding Status reveals the same nine status checkboxes as desktop (Estimate, Approved, In progress, Review, Complete, Invoiced, Paid, Declined, Imported) plus 'Clear selection'.
2. After 'Apply filters' the sheet closes and the work order list shows only the ticked statuses.
3. The reopened sheet's title shows the applied-filter count, for example 'All Filters (1)', and the Status accordion header is highlighted with the selected values ticked.
column8: requirements.md Story 12 S12-R2; S12-R3; Story 2 S2-R1

column1: Tapping an individual filter chip on mobile opens that filter's own sheet with an 'Apply filter' button
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
column6:
1. Tap the Status chip (not All Filters).
2. Read the sheet.
3. Tick a status and tap the bottom button.
column7:
1. A bottom sheet opens for that single filter: its title row shows the filter's icon and name (for example 'Status') with a close (x) button - no accordion list of the other filters.
2. The sheet shows only that filter's options (the nine status checkboxes plus 'Clear selection').
3. The bottom button reads 'Apply filter' (singular); tapping it applies the selection and filters the list.

column1: The mobile Customer filter has search, multi-select and removable tags, matching desktop
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page; several customers exist.
3. The All Filters sheet is open with the Customer accordion expanded.
column6:
1. Type part of a customer name in the 'Search customer' field and watch the list.
2. Select two or three customers.
3. Look at the input area and the list rows.
4. Remove one customer with the x on its tag, then tap 'Apply filters'.
column7:
1. The list narrows to matching names as you type.
2. Each selected customer appears as a tag with an x in the input area, and its list row shows a checkmark.
3. Removing a tag deselects just that customer.
4. After 'Apply filters' the list shows only work orders of the remaining selected customers, and the sheet title counts the applied filters (for example 'All Filters (2)').

column1: The mobile Lead Technician and Service Advisor filters offer their search lists in the sheet
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page; technicians and advisors exist.
3. The All Filters sheet is open.
column6:
1. Expand the Lead Technician accordion row and look at its content.
2. Collapse it, expand the Service Advisor row and look at its content.
3. Select one name in either list and tap 'Apply filters'.
column7:
1. The Lead Technician row opens with a 'Search technician' field and the technician list.
2. The Service Advisor row opens with a 'Search advisor' field and the advisor list.
3. Applying a selection filters the work order list just like on desktop.
column8: requirements.md Story 12 S12-R2; Story 4 S4-R1; Story 5 S5-R1

column1: The mobile Asset on site filter offers Yes/No with Clear selection in the sheet
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page; work orders exist in both on-site states.
3. The All Filters sheet is open.
column6:
1. Expand the Asset on site accordion row.
2. Choose Yes and tap 'Apply filters'.
3. Look at the list.
column7:
1. The Asset on site row opens showing the two options Yes and No plus 'Clear selection'.
2. Only one option can be selected at a time.
3. After applying, the list shows only work orders matching the chosen on-site state.

column1: Active chips and Clear filters behave on mobile the same way as on desktop
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with at least one filter applied via the sheet.
column6:
1. Look at the chip row after applying the filter.
2. Look for a 'Clear filters' control while a filter is active.
3. Use it and look at the chips and the list.
column7:
1. The chip for the applied filter shows the active state with the selected value(s), like on desktop.
2. A 'Clear filters' control appears while at least one filter is active.
3. Using it removes all active filters, the chips return to default and the full list comes back.
column8: requirements.md Story 12 S12-R2; Story 7 S7-R1/R3; Story 8 S8-R1

column1: Mobile has no collapse toggle: the filter chip row is always visible
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
column6:
1. Look at the toolbar row (Search, sort icon, New Work Order button).
2. Look for any control that would hide the filter chip row.
column7:
1. There is no filter-bar collapse/expand (funnel) toggle on mobile.
2. The filter chip row is always visible on the mobile Work Orders page.

column1: Filters matching no work orders on mobile show the same empty state as desktop
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page; work orders exist.
column6:
1. Apply a filter combination that matches no work orders (for example a customer plus a status that customer never has).
2. Look at the list area.
column7:
1. The list shows the same no-results empty state as desktop, saying no results were found for the current filters.
2. The empty state includes the prompt to clear filters.
3. No error appears.

column1: The work order list request carries the active filter selections
column5:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser with developer tools open on the Network tab.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with no filters applied.
column6:
1. Apply a Status selection and a Customer selection in the filter bar.
2. In the Network tab, find the work order list request the page sends after the change.
3. Inspect the request's parameters.
column7:
1. The list request includes the active filter selections as request parameters (status values and customer identifiers).
2. The request succeeds (HTTP 200).
3. The response contains only work orders matching the filters - the filtering is done by the backend, not just hidden client-side.
column8: requirements.md Story 2 S2-R2; Story 3 S3-R6 (backend view)

column1: A combined multi-filter request returns only work orders matching all filters, any value within each filter
column5:
1. You are signed in with developer tools open on the Network tab.
2. Seeded ZZAUTOTEST work orders exist: customer A with an Estimate and an Approved work order, customer B with an Estimate work order.
column6:
1. On the Work Orders page apply Status = Estimate + Approved and Customer = customer A.
2. Capture the resulting list request and response.
column7:
1. One request carries both filters together (both statuses and the customer).
2. The response returns customer A's Estimate and Approved work orders only.
3. Customer B's work orders are absent - the customer filter and status filter both restrict the result, while the two statuses combine as either-or.
column8: requirements.md Story 2 S2-R2; Story 3 S3-R6; Story 8 S8-R3 (backend view)

column1: A list request with a deleted or unknown filter value is handled without a server error
column5:
1. You are signed in and can replay/edit the work order list request (developer tools or an API client).
2. You have a captured filtered list request, and one of its filter values has since been deleted (for example a removed ZZAUTOTEST customer) or is a made-up identifier.
column6:
1. Send the list request containing the no-longer-existing (or made-up) filter value.
2. Inspect the HTTP status and the response body.
column7:
1. The backend does not fail with a server error (no HTTP 5xx).
2. The response is a normal, successful list response - the invalid value is ignored or simply matches nothing.
3. Any still-valid filter values in the same request are applied normally.

column1: A list request with malformed filter parameters does not produce a server error
column5:
1. You are signed in and can replay/edit the work order list request.
2. You have a captured filtered list request to tamper with.
column6:
1. Corrupt the filter parameters (wrong types, scrambled values, nonsense text) and send the request.
2. Inspect the HTTP status and the response body.
3. Also open the equally malformed page URL in the browser and watch the page.
column7:
1. The backend responds gracefully - no HTTP 5xx / crash; either a normal (unfiltered or empty) list or a clean validation response.
2. In the browser the page still loads without filters and without an error message, matching the malformed-URL requirement.

column1: A filter combination matching nothing returns a successful empty list, not an error
column5:
1. You are signed in with developer tools open on the Network tab.
2. A filter combination is known to match no work orders (for example a seeded customer plus a status they never have).
column6:
1. Apply that filter combination on the Work Orders page.
2. Capture the list request and response.
column7:
1. The request succeeds (HTTP 200).
2. The response contains an empty result set (zero work orders) - an empty match is a normal outcome, not an error.
3. The page renders the no-results empty state from this response.
